title: OpenAI, Google pushing new AI models easily tricked into making nudes, researchers say
gist: White Circle's red-teaming found guardrails of DALL-E 3, Nano Banana 2 and GPT-Image-2 can be bypassed about 13% of the time using free tools, and newer releases from OpenAI and Google appear more breakable. The firm uses this to argue for mandatory independent third-party AI safety testing, as AI-generated CSAM findings rise sharply.

themes.theme: RISE jailbreak results on leading image models

insights.claim: White Circle researchers bypassed safety filters of DALL-E 3, Google's Nano Banana 2 and GPT-Image-2 about 13 percent of the time using off-the-shelf tools and API calls, the highest bypass rate of any method tested under the same standard.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Quantifies guardrail weakness at frontier labs, creating reputational and regulatory exposure for Google and OpenAI.

insights.claim: The RISE attack pipeline uses a downloaded Qwen model to generate jailbreaks and Gemini 3.8 Flash as judge, showing frontier defenses can be broken without frontier models or proprietary tech.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Cheap automated red-teaming lowers the cost of attacks and implies defenses need continuous adversarial testing.
insights.quote: You don't need to have frontier models to break defenses of a frontier model, which is very interesting

insights.claim: White Circle says the newer ChatGPT Images 2.5 and Nano Banana 2.1 are significantly more breakable than predecessors, hypothesizing either greater capability or safety being deprioritized in favor of capability.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: If capability gains erode safety, release cadence may create liability and regulatory risk; neither company responded.
insights.quote: either the newer models are more sophisticated and capable of generating a wider range of content, or that safety has been deprioritized in favor of capability
insights.locator: Meanwhile, OpenAI and Google have released new models

insights.claim: White Circle's CEO says the weakness on easy-to-spot categories like explicit content bodes poorly for defenses against more serious misuse such as hacking.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Failures on simple categories raise doubts about frontier labs' broader safety claims.
insights.locator: White Circle's attack method can break down

insights.claim: White Circle's engineer says image-generator red-teaming is 'very poorly calibrated' with 'literally zero papers' setting norms and is plagued by reporting issues.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Lack of standard benchmarks makes lab safety claims hard to compare or verify.
insights.locator: A lot of time was invested

themes.theme: Case for mandatory third-party safety testing

insights.claim: Shilov argues frontier labs will not invest in safety testing until it is mandatory, that labs shouldn't assess their own safety, and that governments should push independent third-party evaluation, even nuclear-style third-party monitoring.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Pushes toward regulatory mandates for external audits, a potential cost and compliance driver for AI labs.
insights.quote: the labs building these systems are the ones assessing their own safety, publishing their own results, and setting their own standards

insights.claim: White Circle says AI safety work is often compromised because anyone doing interesting safety work is likely to be contracted by frontier labs, and it found Anthropic's bug bounty too constrained, focused on universal jailbreaks in domains Anthropic defines.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Independence of evaluators is a structural weakness; a market may emerge for truly independent safety auditors.
insights.locator: White Circle has partnered with frontier labs

insights.claim: OpenAI and Anthropic reportedly urged that external evaluators sign restrictive NDAs to prevent trade secret leaks, which White Circle says it would refuse, likely ending any Anthropic partnership if required.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: NDA terms for outside evaluators will shape how much public safety evidence emerges.
insights.locator: Anthropic has proposed going one step further

insights.claim: White Circle plans to open-source the full attack pipeline and present at NeurIPS 2026 in November, which could increase scrutiny on Google and OpenAI later this fall.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: A catalyst for press and regulatory attention on image-model safety.

insights.claim: The IWF found 6,310 AI images meeting the legal definition of CSAM in the first half of 2026, about 40 percent above all of 2025, including imagery of children under two.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Sharp growth strengthens the political case for mandatory model-level safeguards and UK-style safety frameworks.
insights.locator: Last week, the Internet Watch Foundation

insights.claim: A Google co-authored study found that 20 percent of people who admitted to making AI nudes did so 'for fun' or as a joke and nearly a third were experimenting, so model-level friction may deter a subset of perpetrators.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Supports mandatory guardrails at accessible mainstream models, meaning weaker filters carry real harm.

insights.claim: Google's July study concluded the most critical intervention point is at the source: the AI tools used to make fake sexual images, since non-consensual content is mostly shared in private channels where it is less likely to be detected.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Regulatory focus is likely to land on tool developers rather than distribution platforms.
insights.locator: This non-consensual content is commonly shared
